newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to let Jews occupy 100 West Bank homes.
newsitem.headline: Israel to let Jews occupy 100 West Bank homes.

text.p: An Israeli spokesman said on Thursday the government had given Jewish settlers permission to occupy another 100 West Bank homes and many Israelis wanted to move to the occupied territories.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's aide David Bar-Illan said permits had been given for Jews to live in 100 homes built in the Jewish settlement of Kedumim, near Nablus, in the north of the occupied West Bank.

Israel's previous government, under its drive for peace with the Arabs, denied the permits when it came to power in 1992. Netanyahu took power in June, backing more settlement and vowing to reverse the land-for-peace policy of his predecessors.

"There are 100 housing units that have been built which are there and for which permits to live in have been given, another 100 units which are at a stage of foundation-laying and for which licenses have been requested," Bar-Illan told Reuters.
In Kedumim, witnesses said some of the homes had been occupied for a while by settlers apparently lacking permits.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat has condemned the settlement policy but said on Thursday he was ready to meet the Israeli leader to discuss implementing a long-overdue self-rule deal on the occupied city of Hebron.
It would be their first meeting in more than two months but both sides said no date had been set. Netanyahu has sought amendments to the Hebron deal signed by the previous Israeli government.
Israel's Peace Now movement accused Netanyahu of misleading the world and endangering peace with a settlement policy that has angered Arabs and hurt Israel's image in the West.
In Europe this week, Netanyahu said his government had been falsely accused of unbridled settlement but added: "I can only say I wish that were true."
The U.S. State Department said last month that settlement expansion was not helpful to peace negotiations.
Some 130,000 Jews live in guarded enclaves among the more than two million Palestinians of the West Bank and Gaza captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.
Bar-Illan denied an Israel Radio report Kedumim had approval to build 700 more homes but defended expansion.

"This consists of two elements, the natural increase through birth...and also the fact that there are many people who want to move into these areas and of course the government will do nothing to prevent that," he said.
Under Netanyahu's predecessors Yitzhak Rabin and Shimon Peres, Israel handed over parts of the occupied territories to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's self-rule authority.

Arafat's PLO said this week Israeli policies would reignite violence and isolate the Jewish state at a time when talks were deadlocked over Hebron, a tense West Bank town where 400 Jews live amid 100,000 Arabs.
The U.N. General Assembly called on Wednesday for the immediate acceleration of negotiations.

But Israel's newspaper Haaretz said that next Sunday a plan would be presented to the Jerusalem district planning committee to build Jewish housing in the middle of Ras al Amud neighbourhood of Arab East Jerusalem, also occupied in 1967.
Oman said on Wednesday it had frozen ties with Israel over what it said was the Jewish state's failure to keep commitments to the Palestinian leadership.
